title: Paul Graham on picking founders, honesty with investors, and why forecasts don't matter
summary: At a Revenue Boot Camp fireside chat with Mike Moritz and Guy Kawasaki, Paul Graham explains what YC looks for in early founders. He stresses people who build because they love it, candor with smart investors, and building something people want over spreadsheet forecasts.

principles.text: Back founders who build for fun, not duty. Ask what they made outside work or school.
principles.quote: the big question we ask is what have you made outside of school or work because you liked it because if you don't like it you're not going to do well as a startup founder

principles.text: Be candid with smart investors, like telling a doctor your symptoms. They will catch a lie.
principles.quote: the better the investor the more it should be like going to the doctor like don't lie about your symptoms tell them exactly what's going on

principles.text: The best financial forecast is building something people really want; the money follows.
principles.quote: I think the best financial forecast is a sense that you're developing something that people will really care and want and if they really care and want the money will follow

principles.text: Ideally build something you yourself want to use; next best is something someone close to you wants.
principles.quote: it's ideal if they're building something they themselves want to use the next best thing is something you know that someone very close to them like their wife or sibling wants to use

principles.text: Predict winning platforms by watching what hackers themselves use, since they build for those platforms.
principles.quote: look for the platforms that hackers themselves use and those are the ones exciting things are going to happen to you

principles.text: A startup isn't dead until the founders give up; early on they can morph it into anything.
principles.quote: as long as the founders haven't given up they can morph the company into anything
